sections.h2: Who bills and collects in Monroe County
sections.html:
In the Keys, valuation and collection sit in separate buildings. One elected office decides what a parcel is worth and who gets an exemption. Another prints the notices and takes the payments. A seller in Key West and a seller in Key Largo deal with the same two offices at different counters.

The sequence runs like this: the appraiser's January value, combined with millage from the commission and other taxing bodies, becomes the roll certified for collection. Notices go to the address of record on that roll. Escrow lenders request the bill themselves, so the owner may only receive a copy.

Under Statute 197.122, the owner is responsible for learning what is due and paying before delinquency, bill or no bill. A separate bill goes out for each parcel, matched to the way the deed is recorded, so an owner of two lots should expect two notices.

If a bill never arrives, do not wait. Call the collector, confirm the address of record, and ask for a reprinted statement. Late payment carries the same delinquency date whether or not you received the mailing.

sections.h2: Housing in the Keys at a glance
sections.html: Monroe County had 80,406 residents in mid-2025 across 983.04 square miles of land. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $780,600, and 65.8 percent of the 56,009 housing units are lived in by their owners. Median rent is $1,999 a month. Seniors make up 27.2 percent of the county, so the senior and homestead programs below get heavy use.

The tax collector runs five offices along the Keys, and each one handles property tax.

sections.h2: How to prepare an appeal or correction
sections.html:
Start with the August proposed-tax notice. A value challenge uses a DR-486 petition that the clerk must receive within 25 days, so write the deadline on the notice the day it arrives.

A denied exemption has its own 30 day petition clock. Owners of furnished rentals or business equipment also file Form DR-405 by April 1.

  • Gather recent sales of similar properties on your island or key before you file.
  • Photograph any damage that existed on January 1, since value is set on that date.
  • Keep the notice and your filing receipt together.

You can also ask the appraiser for the comparable sales behind your value.

Statements normally mail by November 1, and March is the last month at full price.

  • November: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent, and February brings 1 percent.
  • March: the gross amount, no discount.

On April 1 an unpaid account turns delinquent, and tax certificates are sold by June 1. Instead of a lump sum, owners can ask about a quarterly installment plan, a statutory partial payment plan or a homestead tax deferral program. The application date for these is May 1.

sections.h2: Homestead and Save Our Homes in a Keys sale
sections.html:
A capped assessment belongs to the owner and ends when the house sells. With a typical owned home valued at $780,600, the distance between a long-held capped value and a fresh assessment can be wide.

The exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value if filed by March 1. Yearly growth in assessed value is held below the lesser of 3 percent or CPI, which the state chart pegs at 2.7 percent for 2026. After a sale, the next January 1 assessment starts from just value for the new owner. If you are buying again in Florida, ask the appraiser about portability, which has a three year window.

With a large senior population, relief tied to age and military service comes up often. The state offers a $5,000 assessed value reduction for a disabled ex-servicemember, a homestead discount for qualifying veteran owners 65 and older, and a possible total exemption for permanent and total disability.

Seniors may also benefit from an optional local ordinance. Ask the property appraiser whether Monroe County or a city in it has adopted one, and what income limit applies.

sections.h2: Taxes and deed costs at a Keys closing
sections.html:
The title company usually divides the sale year's tax between the parties on the settlement statement. A spring or summer closing happens before that year's bill exists, so the figure is an estimate.

Keys deeds carry state stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of price (section 201.02), unlike Miami-Dade. Payment goes to the clerk, whose recording charges under section 28.24 start at $5.00 for the first page.

Unpaid taxes lead to a certificate sale and, years later, a clerk-run deed auction. Pay off any open year before closing.

On closing day, expect the title company to confirm payoffs, collect your signature on the deed in front of a notary and witnesses, and send the deed to the clerk for recording. Keep a copy of the settlement statement for your own tax records.

sections.h2: Getting ready to list a Keys home
sections.html:
A few routine steps help. Pull the parcel record and check the owner name and mailing address. Collect the last statement for each parcel you own, since a two-lot sale involves two bills. Ask the collector's office for a payoff on any open year, and ask your title company for a proration estimate. If you rented the home furnished, confirm whether a business equipment return is outstanding. Write down every phone number and name of the office you spoke with, along with the date. Share the paperwork with your closing agent early so the settlement statement holds no surprises.

A buyer who pays cash can skip lender requirements, but the same taxes, liens and recorded documents still have to be sorted out before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When does the Monroe County bill stop being penalty free?
faqs.a: Pay by March 31. That is when the gross amount falls due, and April 1 starts delinquency. Earlier payment, November through February, shrinks the bill by 4, 3, 2 or 1 percent.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about a lost Monroe County bill?
faqs.a: The tax collector, at (305) 295-5044. Each parcel gets its own bill, matched to the deed as recorded.

faqs.q: Does a Keys homeowner's capped value go to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The buyer's first assessment starts at just value. You may be able to carry part of the savings to your next Florida homestead through portability.

faqs.q: Can I pay Monroe County taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, through the tax collector's quarterly installment plan, a statutory partial payment option or a homestead deferral. State guidance sets May 1 as the application date.

faqs.q: Who runs a tax deed auction in Monroe County?
faqs.a: The county clerk holds the auction, so overbid or surplus questions go to the clerk.
